findings.finding: The plan says `BARE_REMOTE_UPKEEP_PINS` is `gc.autoDetach=false, maintenance.autoDetach=false`. The dict actually has a third key, `receive.autogc=false`, and `apply_upkeep_pins` writes all three. Step 1 will therefore also set `receive.autogc=false` on the tracker. This does no harm and adds no new key, but the plan's account of what the call does is incomplete.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the new test, positively assert the fixture's trace records the fixture's `git commit` and a `git maintenance run --auto` child (with `--no-detach` or without `--detach`) before asserting the absence of `--detach`.
evidence: "Positive control, built inline ... Then, with a fresh trace, `_cli_tracker` records no such child with `--detach`."
findings.finding: The negative assertion ('records no such child with `--detach`') passes vacuously if no trace is written. This can happen if the fixture's git subprocess uses a scrubbed or explicit env that drops `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`, or if maintenance is not spawned at all. The inline positive control uses a different code path, so it does not guard against this.
scenarios: `_cli_tracker` calls git with `env={...}` built from a fixed dict, so the trace env var never reaches the fixture's commit.
findings.suggested_fix: After building `_cli_tracker` with a fresh trace, assert that `maintenance_children(trace)` is non-empty. Then assert that every child argv lacks the exact element `--detach`, preferably that it contains `--no-detach`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In test_cli_tracker_leaves_no_detached_upkeep, assert that the `_cli_tracker` trace records at least one `git maintenance run` child and that every such child carries `--no-detach`, not just that none carries `--detach`.
evidence: Plan: "Then, with a fresh trace, `_cli_tracker` records no such child with `--detach`."
tests/unit/test_authorship_fixture_maintenance.py:64-65 asserts `maintenance_children, "fixture did not exercise Git auto-maintenance"` and `all("--no-detach" in argv ...)`.
tests/_git_upkeep.py:106-114: `_trace_events` returns nothing for an unwritten trace, so `maintenance_children` returns [] and a pure negative check passes.
findings.finding: The `_cli_tracker` half of the new test only asserts that no `git maintenance run` child carries `--detach`. That passes vacuously if the fixture's trace records no maintenance child at all, or nothing at all: for example, if a later edit gives the fixture an explicit env that drops GIT_TRACE2_EVENT, or the commit stops reaching auto maintenance. The positive control runs on a different repository, so it cannot prove the fixture's own commit was observed. The existing sibling test requires a maintenance child to be present and checks that every one carries `--no-detach`.
scenarios: A future edit passes an explicit env to the fixture's subprocess calls that drops GIT_TRACE2_EVENT. The trace stays empty and the test still passes while the fixture is no longer observed.
The fixture's commit stops reaching auto maintenance in some environment. The negative check passes without showing that the pins took effect.
findings.suggested_fix: After building `_cli_tracker` under the fresh trace: `children = maintenance_children(trace); assert children, "fixture commit did not exercise auto maintenance"; assert all("--no-detach" in argv for argv in children), children`. This follows tests/unit/test_authorship_fixture_maintenance.py.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the new test gets the trace/config env in place before `_cli_tracker`'s commit runs (e.g. it is a factory or plain function called in the body, or env is set in an earlier-ordered fixture), consistent with the no-new-helper constraint.
evidence: "The fixture `_cli_tracker` builds the tracker"
"With `monkeypatch.setenv` it sets `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` ... Then, with a fresh trace, `_cli_tracker` records no such child"
"No new ... test helper is added"
findings.finding: The new test's ordering is ambiguous and may be impossible as written. If `_cli_tracker` is a regular pytest fixture, it executes before the test body. Its `git commit` would then run before the body's `monkeypatch.setenv(GIT_TRACE2_EVENT/GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/...)`, so the trace would never capture the fixture's commit. A fixture also cannot be called directly from the test body.
scenarios: The executor requests `_cli_tracker` as a test parameter. The fixture commit runs untraced, the trace file is empty, and the negative assertion passes without exercising anything.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the minimum git version the new test assumes (or the CI git version) and skip with a reason when `git --version` is below the version that emits `--detach`/`--no-detach` for auto maintenance.
evidence: "A GIT_TRACE2_EVENT trace of that commit on this host (git 2.56.0) records one child: `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach`"
findings.finding: The positive control assumes git passes an explicit `--detach` to the auto-maintenance child. This was measured only on git 2.56.0 on one host. Older git versions spawn `git maintenance run --auto --quiet` without a `--detach` flag and detach inside gc via `gc.autoDetach`. On such a host the control would fail, or a looser assertion would become meaningless. The plan states no minimum git version or guard.
scenarios: CI runner with an older distro git: the control assertion fails although the fix is correct.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the commit SHA, run timestamp and `make verify` exit code (with log path) will be recorded on the ticket as AC 4's attestation.
evidence: "exit status and log live outside the repository"
findings.finding: The `[non-codebase]` make-verify AC names its environment and instrument, but does not say what attestation will be recorded on the ticket. Examples would be the pushed commit SHA, a timestamp, and the exit code or log location. The rule requires such a record for the AC to count as complete.
scenarios: A reviewer cannot confirm which commit the green `make verify` ran against.
findings.suggested_fix: Append to AC 4: 'attestation: comment on ticket with commit SHA, UTC timestamp, exit code 0, log path'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the new test invokes the tracker-building logic after its env is set (e.g. a plain builder function the fixture wraps, or a fixture that depends on the env-setting fixture). Require the pinned trace to contain the fixture's `git maintenance run` child with exact argv element `--no-detach` (or an exited foreground child), not merely the absence of `--detach`.
evidence: "Then, with a fresh trace, `_cli_tracker` records no such child with `--detach`."
"With `monkeypatch.setenv` it sets `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` to a per-test trace file"
"The fixture `_cli_tracker` builds the tracker with a raw `git commit`."
findings.finding: The new test sets GIT_TRACE2_EVENT and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL with `monkeypatch.setenv` inside the test, then checks that `_cli_tracker` records no detached maintenance child. `_cli_tracker` is a pytest fixture. If the test requests it as a parameter, it runs before the setenv calls, so no trace is written for its commit and the 'no --detach child' check passes vacuously. Calling the fixture function directly is rejected by pytest. Separately, an empty or unrelated trace also satisfies 'records no such child', and a substring match on 'detach' would wrongly hit the pinned `--no-detach` argv.
scenarios: The test takes `_cli_tracker` as a parameter, so the fixture's commit runs before GIT_TRACE2_EVENT is set. The trace file stays empty and the assertion passes even if the pins were removed.
The pins are later dropped from the fixture, but the trace path was never captured, so the test stays green and the original flake returns undetected.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the negative half assert a positive fact: the trace contains a `git maintenance run` child whose argv includes exactly `--no-detach` and does not include `--detach` (element equality). Ensure the env is applied before the tracker is built, e.g. factor the body of `_cli_tracker` into a plain function that both the fixture and the test call.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the positive control robust to the git version: either gate the `--detach` argv assertion on a measured git version (≥2.47) with an explicit skip reason, or assert detach via a version-independent trace signal (e.g. a daemonized child or detached `gc --auto`). State the minimum git version the test supports.
evidence: "A GIT_TRACE2_EVENT trace of that commit on this host (git 2.56.0) records one child: `git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach`."
"`git init` plus `git commit --allow-empty` without the pins records a `git maintenance run` child with `--detach`"
The supported matrix includes Linux and CI under any provider, where the system git may predate 2.47.
findings.finding: The positive control assumes git's auto maintenance passes an explicit `--detach` argv to a `git maintenance run` child. The plan measured this only on git 2.56.0. The `maintenance.autoDetach` config and explicit `--detach` passing exist only from roughly git 2.47. Older git, which is common on Linux distros and CI runner images, runs `git maintenance run --auto --quiet` with no `--detach`, and detaching happens inside `git gc --auto` via `gc.autoDetach`. On such hosts the control finds no child with `--detach` and the new test fails, although the pinned fixture is correct.
scenarios: A Linux CI runner or workstation with distro git 2.39 or 2.43: the positive-control assertion fails because the argv has no `--detach`, and `make verify` goes red on a correct fix.

An older-git host: the detached daemon comes from `git gc --auto` (covered by the `gc.autoDetach=false` pin), but the test's argv-shape oracle cannot observe it, so the control is wrong rather than the fixture.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make AC 2's proving command concrete: name the exact runner and loop (e.g. `for i in $(seq 200); do pytest -n 4 tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_fsck_keyset_prev.py || exit 1; done`). Then either show it can fail pre-fix, or reword it as a non-regression soak and state that AC 1 is the discriminating proof.
evidence: "Run alone it passed 6/6."
"Load (4 xdist workers) widens the window, which is why it shows only under `make verify`."
"The flaky test and the rest of the module pass 200 consecutive runs under `pytest -n 4`."
findings.finding: AC 2 does not discriminate between broken and fixed code. The flake reproduced only under full `make verify` load and passed 6/6 when run alone, yet AC 2 reruns only the module under `-n 4`. That run may pass 200/200 even without the fix. The AC also names no runner (pytest-repeat `--count`, a shell loop, or `--flake-finder`), and gives no pre-fix baseline.
scenarios: The executor runs the loop and it passes 200/200, but the same loop would also have passed before the fix.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the tmp gitconfig (or env `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*`) supplies commit identity and disables signing, so both commits succeed under the isolated config.
evidence: "`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` to a tmp gitconfig forcing `maintenance.auto=true`, `maintenance.autoDetach=true`, `gc.autoDetach=true`, and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`"
findings.finding: Pointing `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` at a tmp gitconfig that only sets maintenance/gc keys, together with `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, removes any host `user.name`/`user.email`. The inline `git commit --allow-empty` and the fixture's commit may then fail with an identity error, unless identity comes from env or `-c`. The plan does not state where identity comes from.

findings.suggested_fix: Add `user.name`, `user.email` and `commit.gpgsign=false` to the tmp gitconfig written by the new test.

findings.finding: The positive control assumes that `git init` plus `git commit --allow-empty` will succeed and produce a `maintenance run --detach` child. Nothing makes that commit succeed: the test points `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` at a temp gitconfig that only sets maintenance and gc keys, and sets `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`. That hides the host's user.name and user.email. tests/conftest.py sets no `GIT_AUTHOR_*` or `GIT_COMMITTER_*` variables. Unlike `_cli_tracker` (lines 135-136), the inline control sets no local `user.email` or `user.name`.
scenarios: On a CI or container host whose hostname has no domain, git cannot guess an email address and stops with 'Author identity unknown' or 'unable to auto-detect email address'. The control commit fails before any trace is written, so the new test fails for a reason unrelated to the fix.
findings.suggested_fix: In step 2, add `[user] name = Test, email = test@example.com` to the temp gitconfig, or run `git config user.email/user.name` in the control repo before `git commit --allow-empty`. Either way matches what `_cli_tracker` already does.

findings.finding: The inline positive control (`git init` plus `git commit --allow-empty` without the pins) runs with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL pointed at a tmp gitconfig holding only maintenance/gc keys, and with GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1. That hides the host's user.name and user.email. The plan does not give the control repo an identity; `_cli_tracker` sets one locally at lines 135-136, but the control repo is built separately. subprocess_env sets no GIT_AUTHOR_* or GIT_COMMITTER_* variables, and tests/conftest.py sets no GIT_ variables. On a host whose hostname has no domain part (typical of CI containers), git cannot auto-detect an email and `git commit` exits non-zero, so the test errors before reaching any assertion.
scenarios: CI or container host with a bare hostname: the control commit fails with 'unable to auto-detect email address' and the new test errors.
A developer machine whose only identity is in ~/.gitconfig: masked by GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, so the outcome depends on the host's hostname.

Evidence class: Partially-verified. git's identity fallback is documented behaviour, but whether it succeeds on the CI/verify host is unconfirmed and depends on the hostname.
findings.finding: The positive-control repository in the new test runs `git commit --allow-empty` with global and system git config replaced (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL set to a tmp file, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1). The plan gives it no committer identity. `_cli_tracker` sets user.email and user.name locally, but the inline control repo does not. git will then try to work out an identity from user@hostname, and the commit fails with 'unable to auto-detect email address' on hosts whose hostname has no domain. The control would then error out (or, if unchecked, record no maintenance child) instead of proving that detached upkeep happens.

scenarios: A Linux CI or container host whose hostname has no FQDN: the control `git commit --allow-empty` fails with 'Author identity unknown', so the new test errors.
